summary.text: SAFFIRE-II is a spacecraft fire experiment run on a Cygnus vehicle that aims to determine large-scale fire growth rate and flammability limits in low gravity.

fuels.text: Samples include SIBAL, silicone, structure PMMA, flat PMMA, and PMMA with Nomex.

geometry.text: A sample card containing 9 samples, each 5 cm x 29 cm, is installed in the middle of a large flow duct.

flow.text: Air flow velocity of either 20 or 30 cm/s depending on sample material, concurrent or opposed.

measurements.text: Thermocouples (flow, flame, plume temperatures), radiometers (flame radiation), solid state sensors (pressure, CO2 and O2 mole faction), and anemometers (flow velocity).

claims.text: The investigation aims to determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity.
The investigation aims to investigate low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in the normal gravity material flammability screening test.
The investigation hypothesizes that using terrestrial fires and fire standards to design spacecraft fire safety systems presents an inherent risk because of the significant level of uncertainty.

limitations.text: Sample and experimental parameter details are held in a separate Experimental Details file that is not part of the metadata text.
Only PSI metadata was examined for this card; no document text was processed, so details beyond the metadata fields are not captured.

modeling_resources.description: Experimental table and instrument data (temperature, radiation, pressure, CO2 and O2, flow velocity) could support future predictive modeling. No model is claimed to exist or be validated.
